subject: Capacity allocation request — Helios AI launch window / Mosaic integration
messages:
From: Alan Park <alan@heliosaitech.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@heliosaitech.com, Samantha Ruiz <sam.ruiz@heliosaitech.com>
Date: 2028-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Capacity request for Mosaic launch (timing: Jan 18)

Marcus —

Quick note from Helios' side: we're targeting a public launch of our Mosaic product on Jan 18. The integration with Redwood is central to latency SLAs for initial customers. Based on our load testing, we need a committed 40-GPU slice for inference (NVIDIA H100-equivalent) plus a 20-GPU burst lane for the first 72 hours.

I attached the MOP and a baseline estimate. We understand this is a lot; we want to understand what a guaranteed reservation vs. a burst policy would cost and the fallback behavior if preemption happens. We also need confirmation of model variants you support (int8 vs int4) and any quantization guidance.

Can we lock something before our procurement window (EoY contracting)? Otherwise the launch economics start to wobble.

—Alan
Head of Ops, Helios AI
[attachment: helios_multiproduct_mop_v3.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Park <alan@heliosaitech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-05T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity request for Mosaic launch (timing: Jan 18)

Alan — thanks for the clear ask and the MOP; I skimmed it and shared with Capacity & Solutions. High level: we can support either a dedicated reservation or a reserve-with-burst lane, but the economics and guarantees differ.

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik: can you evaluate current fleet headroom for the week of Jan 15–22 and give two formal options (reservation pricing + SLA, vs burst with preemption credit policy)?
- Lauren: can you flag any CS commitments we should attach to the contract (migration window, launch on-call, playbook)?
- Alan / Helios: please confirm target concurrency/latency p95 and model size (float16 peak tokens/sec) so we size correctly.

If we can get a deal term this quarter (EoY), RevOps can prioritize reservation slots in January. I’ll coordinate internal escalation if we need ad-hoc carve-outs.

—Marcus
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Alan Park <alan@heliosaitech.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-05T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity request for Mosaic launch (timing: Jan 18)

Marcus / Alan —

Quick capacity note after an initial inventory: week of Jan 15 we have two upcoming enterprise starts but there is roughly 120 GPU-equivalents of headroom across the US-West pool. That said, headroom is fragmented by node sizing and hot-path commitments. Operational constraints: we have a handful of long-running Dedicated deals that are non-preemptible and smaller burst lanes already committed for other launches.

Options we can offer (fast summary):

1) Dedicated reservation: 40 GPUs reserved (non-preemptible) for a 6-month term. Cost: +40% to list for reserved pricing due to short lead time and allocation friction. SLA: 99.9% availability in-catalog with scheduled maintenance windows. Requires RevOps-approval and contract amendment.

2) Reserve + burst lane (recommended for timeline risk): Reserve 20 GPUs guaranteed; additional 20 GPUs in a prioritized burst lane that is preemptible by higher-ranked reserved deals. If preempted during the launch window, we issue credits equivalent to X% of hourly reserved rate (we need RevOps input on credit policy). No changes to long-term cluster topology required; faster to provision.

3) Opportunistic spot + traffic shaping: No reservation; instead we provide an autoscale policy with aggressive prefix caching and assisted quantization recommendations. Lowest cost but highest risk to launch SLAs.

For sizing I also need: model param size and expected qps at p95. Alan: your MOP lists 9B and 25 qps/p95 at 512 tokens — confirm. Also attaching our quick capacity model (CSV).

—Karthik
Sr. Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_capacity_model_q4.csv (text/csv)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Alan Park <alan@heliosaitech.com>
Date: 2028-12-05T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity request for Mosaic launch (timing: Jan 18)

Alan / team —

From a CS perspective we should package: a migration playbook (runbook + on-call), an ops dry-run 2 weeks before launch, and an explicit preemption acceptance clause (how many minutes of interruption trigger credits). If Helios takes option 2 (20 reserved + 20 burst), we should include a rolling fallback to a slightly smaller model variant (int4) which Karthik can validate for quality impact.

Also: if RevOps approves a short 6-month reservation, we can include a launch success credit (one week of reduced billing) if availability drops below 99.5% during the 72-hour launch window. That is a product-level concession we should only attach if Sales and Finance sign-off.

—Lauren
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Alan Park <alan@heliosaitech.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-06T08:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity request for Mosaic launch (timing: Jan 18)

Thanks all — we prefer option 2 (20 reserved + 20 burst). We accept a preemption-credit framework but need the following in contract before procurement signs:
- A guarantee of capacity prioritization during our launch window (Jan 17–19) with a defined credit if preemption prevents serving at agreed p95 SLAs.
- A clear escalation contact and on-call window (we'll need a single point in SRE).
- Confirmation that int4 fallback has <3% quality delta for our primary prompt set (we will provide a small eval set).

I'll share the eval set today; please include the proposed credit numbers in the commercial term sheet (RevOps). We can move quickly if the term sheet aligns.

—Alan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-06T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: ticketing for RevOps / leadership sign-off (Helios — option 2)

Team — internal follow-up: Helios verbally committed to option 2. Please open a RevOps expedite ticket and route to Finance for a 6-month carveout pricing and the proposed launch-credit language. Karthik — post the exact credit formula (hourly credit %, measurement window) into the ticket. Lauren — attach the dry-run playbook and on-call roster. Neha — loop in Legal for a short amendment (preemption clause + escalation contacts).

We need to turn the commercial term sheet by EoW to keep Helios in the Jan slot. If we miss it they will consider a cloud partner alternative. I’ll escalate to Ajay if RevOps cannot move quickly.

—Marcus
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
